correctness.rationale: For \(u=\sqrt{17}-4\) and \(c=\sqrt u\), differentiation of the closed fourth power of the universal one-variable bound gives the unique maximizer \(a=c\). The displayed isosceles unit pair and \(\lambda_0=(1-c)/(1+c)\) attain exactly that value in the constructed norm, while the third strip is inactive on the extremizing vector. The third strip is nevertheless nonredundant, so the unit ball is a centrally symmetric hexagon. In dimension two, failure of uniform non-squareness would force a parallelogram unit ball by compactness and the equality geometry of the triangle inequality; hence the hexagonal norm is uniformly non-square. The actual high-precision verifier was inspected and independently corroborates the algebra.

value.rationale: An explicit two-dimensional counterexample to a published all-parameter Banach-space conjecture is a motivated boundary result. The construction also isolates why preserving one extremizing isosceles configuration while trimming an unused corner defeats the conjectured geometry.
residual_risks: The counterexample leaves the exponent-by-exponent classification open.

final_claim: At \(p=4\), the explicit hexagonal norm in the record is uniformly non-square but attains Baronti--Bertella's universal upper bound for the \(p\)-isosceles constant, so their all-\(p\) equality characterization is false already in dimension two.
limitations: It does not classify all \(p>2\) or compute the constructed norm's \(H_p\) for other exponents.
